properties.description:
⭐ THIS IS THE `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself` TEST, APPLIED TO WORK BUILT THE SAME HOUR, AND IT FAILED. Anthony's standing instruction is to ask `find_tools` the question a USER would ask, in their words. Two queries, one job:

    "has the design I depend on moved since I declared it"          → 3rd of 5, found
    "tell me when the other team changes their design so my
     project knows it is out of date"                                → ABSENT from the top 5

In the second, the top hit is `invalidates` — a tool for marking a finding stale, which has nothing to do with the question.

🛑 THE DIAGNOSIS IS `tool_not_found`, NOT `tool_missing`, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT. The capability exists, is verified, and is served. A session that needed it and hand-rolled a `git diff` on somebody else's export instead would be a DISCOVERABILITY failure — a different repair from building anything. `cap:a-session-reports-the-work-it-did-by-hand` exists to catch exactly that class, and this is a case where the failure is predictable in advance rather than discovered afterwards.

⭐ WHY IT FAILS, and it is mechanical rather than mysterious. `find_tools` is BM25 over the served name, description and parameter names. The description is written in this design's own nouns — DEPENDS ON, declaration, upstream, moved. The words a user reaches for are not in it: *other team*, *out of date*, *stale*, *notify*, *tell me when*, *changed*, *sibling*, *partner*. None of those appear anywhere in the served text, so there is nothing for the ranking to match.

⚠️ THE FIX IS WORDING, NOT A TOOL — and it is deliberately NOT applied here, because a description is the surface an agent binds to and `toolsnap` makes every change to it a reviewed artifact. Rewording it is a real change to the shipped surface and belongs in a change somebody looked at, not smuggled in beside the feature it critiques.

⚠️ AND THE SAME MEASUREMENT SHOULD BE RUN ON THE REST OF THE SURFACE BEFORE ANY FIX. One tool reworded is one tool; if the surface is systematically written in reflow2's nouns — which the 164 descriptions plausibly are, since they were all written by people building reflow2 — then the finding is about the SURFACE and a per-tool patch is the wrong shape of repair. Nobody has measured that.

🛑 NOTHING DETECTS THIS. There is no check that a served tool is reachable from the words its users would use, and the third leg of `fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it` — A DETECTOR THAT NOTICES ABSENCE — is missing here exactly as it is elsewhere. This finding was produced by a human instruction followed by hand, not by anything the system does on its own.
properties.name: The upstream watch is findable only by someone who already speaks reflow2 — in a user's own words it does not surface, and an unrelated tool ranks first
properties.statement: MEASURED against the live 164-tool surface the hour it shipped. Asked in reflow2's vocabulary — 'has the design I depend on moved since I declared it' — `upstream_status` ranks 3rd of 5. Asked in a USER's words for the same job — 'tell me when the other team changes their design so my project knows it is out of date' — it does NOT APPEAR IN THE TOP 5 AT ALL, and `invalidates`, an unrelated tool, ranks first.
